qt: to the Commission César Luena (S&D) Subject:

In her State of the Union address of 16 September, President von der Leyen announced the creation of a climate insurance alliance to address the growing gap between climate risks and insurance coverage. Currently, only around 25 % of climate-related economic losses in the EU are covered by insurance. The Commission has announced this initiative – which will bring together insurers, investors, public authorities and other actors – at a time when it is working on a new European climate resilience framework. 1.

How will the new climate insurance alliance be integrated into the upcoming European climate resilience framework and what concrete tools does the Commission envisage to reduce the climate risk protection gap?

What will the Commission do to ensure that growing climate risks do not leave the citizens, businesses and territories most exposed to these threats in a position where they have no coverage options or cannot afford insurance?

Does the Commission hold that improving insurance cover should go hand-in-hand with new European instruments and own resources (an example being a tax on oil and gas company profits) that are specifically designed to finance investments in climate adaptation and risk reduction?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) As a key part of the Climate Resilience Framework, the Climate Insurance Alliance will bring together insurers, reinsurers, insurance intermediaries, insurance takers, risk modelling experts, investors, the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) and public authorities to identify solutions to close the climate insurance gap. By the end 2027, the Alliance will look at and deliver a first set of specific and actionable measures that aim to increase the insurance uptake, incentivise risk prevention and assure adequate insurance capacity. It will also explore possible public-private partnerships at national, regional or European levels to foster the role and uptake of private insurance. The Framework will seek to enhance climate risk management, encouraging moving from a reactive approach to anticipatory, preventive action, thereby reducing exposure of citizens, businesses and territories. Through generating greater risk awareness and improved risk management, the Framework will support improvement in the availability and affordability of insurance. Negotiations on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) are ongoing. The Commission has proposed an overall climate and environmental spending target of 35%, including climate adaptation.
